text: Did something you did in the pantry directly cause the fire alarm to ring?
Were you cooking or heating food in the pantry?
Did the food become burnt or produce smoke, triggering the alarm?
Did steam or water vapor from the food trigger the fire alarm?
Did heat from the food or cooking appliance trigger a heat detector?
Did the cooking appliance itself malfunction or produce something other than smoke, steam, or excess heat that triggered the alarm?
Did the food or cooking create an open flame that activated the fire alarm?
Did cooking produce carbon monoxide that triggered a carbon-monoxide detector linked to the fire alarm?
Did cooking release airborne particles—such as oil or grease aerosol—that triggered the fire alarm?
Were you frying food in oil, producing airborne grease particles that reached a nearby smoke detector and set off the alarm?

I was frying food in oil in the pantry off the hall. The frying released airborne grease particles, which reached a nearby smoke detector and triggered the fire alarm. There was no fire; the alarm was set off by the cooking aerosol.
